svg.title: Small density corrections and exact stabilization of array degrees
svg.desc: A connector from B pi to sheet i has derivative r within exp eta of the target h equals q i over q zero. Set the source density to one and the target density to h divided by r. The corrected derivative is exactly h. Densities are constant on retained blocks, so old derivatives stay fixed. Summable log bounds give an equivalent limiting probability; arrow exhaustion, rather than closure of H, gives an H-valued limiting modulus.

g.text: Correct the unit measure; keep the earlier arrow degrees
Theorems 2.1 and 6.1 · Proposition 5.1 · range-over-source derivative convention
Transport f unchanged along each retained block. Its existing derivatives stay fixed.
All array cell masses remain qᵢ, so μ′ is already a probability.
wₙ → w uniformly, exp(−C) ≤ w ≤ exp(C)
ν = w μ₀ is an equivalent probability.
An old map U keeps δν(Ux, x) = h.
R = ⋃Aₙ gives δν ∈ H on all arrows.
The proof never requires the limiting unit density w to belong to the nonclosed group H.
